headline: Oil fell about 6% to near $110 a barrel as Saudi, Pakistani and Turkish envoys met Iran's leaders to head off new fighting. Currencies barely moved ahead of five central-bank decisions this week.

chapters.title: US Dollar
chapters.teaser: The dollar index slipped about 0.1% to near 101.7 as oil fell sharply on Iran peace efforts. The only US figure this morning, a Chicago Fed gauge of activity for September, came in a little stronger than expected and moved nothing.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: Since the US–Iran war began in February, high oil has kept US inflation up, and markets expect the Federal Reserve to hold this Wednesday and raise rates in December, which supports the dollar. What changed: Over the weekend and into Monday, oil dropped about 6% as Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey sent senior officials to Tehran to stop the fighting flaring again. The Chicago Fed National Activity Index for September rose to +0.07, against about −0.10 expected: a sign the US economy grew slightly faster than its usual pace. Markets ignored it. The 10-year Treasury yield sat near 4.97%, and a Fed hold on Wednesday is priced at about 91–93%. What it means: Cheaper oil eases the inflation worry that keeps a December Fed hike on the table, so it takes a little support away from the dollar. The question to keep asking: does oil keep falling, and does that soften what Federal Reserve policymakers signal on Wednesday?
chapters.fx: What's next: No more major US data today. Coming up: US durable goods orders at 7:30 AM CT and Conference Board consumer confidence at 9:00 AM CT on Tuesday, then the Fed decision at 1:00 PM CT Wednesday, with the press conference at 1:30 PM CT. A hold is priced; the surprise would be a clear signal for or against a December hike.
numbers: Chicago Fed activity index (Sep) +0.07 vs −0.10 expected

scenarios.bull: A new attack on Gulf oil sites or a collapse of the Tehran talks sends oil and US yields back up, lifting the dollar.
scenarios.bear: A ceasefire framework from the Tehran talks pushes oil lower, trims December hike bets and weighs on the dollar.

chapters.title: Euro
chapters.teaser: The euro led the major currencies early on Monday, touching about $1.122, as French borrowing costs eased after Moody's chose not to cut France's credit rating. It slipped back to near $1.120 by the New York open.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: France's debt, a budget fight and street protests pushed its 10-year borrowing cost above 5% last week, near its widest gap over Germany since 2011, which weighed on the euro. What changed: Late Friday, Moody's kept France at Aa3 with a negative outlook, rather than the one-notch cut many expected. French yields eased on Monday. Germany's Ifo business climate survey rose to 90.2 in October, against 90.0 expected, its fifth monthly rise, driven by firms' hopes for the months ahead. The euro gave back its early gain as the morning went on. What it means: Less stress in French bonds removes one weight from the euro, and German firms' brighter outlook helps the case for a European Central Bank hike in December. The question to keep asking: does France get through its budget votes without a new scare?
chapters.fx: What's next: No euro-area data left today. Coming up: France's parliament takes up the revenue part of its budget on Tuesday, then the ECB decides on Thursday at 8:15 AM CT; a hold is expected, with President Christine Lagarde's press conference at about 8:45 AM CT.
numbers: EUR/USD ~1.1196 (−0.1%), after ~1.1219 in the European morning
Moody's: France held at Aa3, negative outlook

scenarios.bull: A smooth French budget vote and an ECB that keeps December open lift the euro toward last week's highs.
scenarios.bear: A new French political scare or a cautious ECB pushes the euro back below $1.12.

chapters.title: British Pound
chapters.teaser: The pound eased to about $1.337 and lost ground to the euro as investors stepped back before Wednesday's UK Budget. A much better-than-expected retail survey from the Confederation of British Industry did not help it.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: A Bank of England rate hike on November 5 is all but priced because UK inflation is running hot, and on Friday the pound hit its strongest against the euro since May 2025. What changed: The CBI's retail sales balance improved to −10 in October from −55, far better than the −47 expected: sales are still falling, but at the slowest pace since April 2025. Even so, the pound slipped about 0.3% against the euro to near 84 pence and dipped to about $1.335 in London trade, as investors avoided big bets before Chancellor Healey presents his first Budget. What it means: The move reflects caution before a big event, not new weakness in the economy. The Budget matters because heavier borrowing could worry bond investors, while tighter spending would cool growth and the case for more Bank of England hikes. The question to keep asking: does the Budget calm or rattle UK bond markets?
chapters.fx: What's next: No UK data left today. Coming up: the UK Budget on Wednesday, around 7:30 AM CT, then the Bank of England decision on November 5, where a hike is about 94% priced.
numbers: EUR/GBP ~0.837 at the New York open (~0.840 in London), from ~0.836 Friday

scenarios.base: The pound stays quiet until the Budget on Wednesday.
scenarios.bull: A Budget that keeps borrowing in check calms gilts and lets the pound recover against the euro.
scenarios.bear: A Budget seen as loosening spending or raising borrowing pushes gilt yields up for the wrong reasons and weighs on the pound.

chapters.title: Japanese Yen
chapters.teaser: The yen weakened slightly, with the dollar up about 0.2% to near ¥157.1, as calmer markets and falling oil cut demand for safe places to park money. The Bank of Japan decides on Friday.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: Japan imports nearly all its energy, so high oil has weighed on the yen this year; last week a global stock wobble briefly lifted it to a one-month high, with the dollar near ¥156.1. What changed: With stock futures rising and oil sliding on the Tehran peace efforts, investors had less reason to hold the yen for safety, and the dollar edged back above ¥157. Cheaper oil helps Japan's trade balance, which is good for the yen over time, but on the day the calmer mood mattered more. What it means: The yen now leans on the Bank of Japan. Japan's core inflation is back above the bank's 2% goal, and a December hike is widely expected; a clear signal of it on Friday would support the yen. The question to keep asking: does the Bank of Japan say a December hike is coming?
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: Japan's services producer prices at 6:50 PM CT tonight, Tokyo consumer prices at 6:30 PM CT Wednesday, and the Bank of Japan decision on Friday, Japan time (late Thursday night CT), where a hold is expected.

scenarios.base: The dollar holds around ¥157 until the Fed and Bank of Japan decisions.
scenarios.bull: A Bank of Japan that clearly signals a December hike, or a fresh stock sell-off, pulls the dollar back toward ¥156.
scenarios.bear: A cautious Bank of Japan and firm US yields lift the dollar toward ¥158.

chapters.title: Swiss Franc
chapters.teaser: The franc was one of the few currencies to gain against the dollar, which slipped about 0.2% to near 0.824 francs. There is no Swiss data until Wednesday.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: The Swiss National Bank holds rates at zero with inflation near zero, so the franc moves mostly on global fear, and it held near a one-month high against the dollar last week. What changed: The dollar was weakest against the franc this morning, at about 0.824, from about 0.825 on Friday, even as calmer markets eased demand for safety elsewhere. The move is small and came with no Swiss news. What it means: With no Swiss data or central-bank news, the franc is following the dollar's dip rather than a change in Switzerland. The question to keep asking: does a calmer Middle East take away the franc's safe-haven support?
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: the UBS survey of Swiss economic expectations on Wednesday at 4:00 AM CT, and the KOF economic barometer on Friday. The Swiss National Bank's next decision is December 10.

scenarios.base: The franc stays near its recent highs while the dollar drifts before the Fed.
scenarios.bull: A flare-up in the Middle East or a stock sell-off pushes the dollar further below 0.82 francs.
scenarios.bear: A peace deal and rising stocks cool the safe-haven demand and lift the dollar back toward 0.83.

chapters.title: Australian Dollar
chapters.teaser: The Australian dollar held near 70.3 US cents, flat on the day, as traders waited for Australia's third-quarter inflation figures on Tuesday evening, CT. Those figures will likely decide whether the central bank raises rates next week.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: The Reserve Bank of Australia has raised rates four times this year to 4.60%, and markets see a November 3 hike as close to an even bet, which has kept the Aussie near its strongest levels of the year. What changed: Over the weekend, Reserve Bank of Australia assistant governor Sarah Hunter said the job on inflation is not done after four hikes, keeping a November hike in view. Cheaper oil today slightly eases the inflation picture but did not move the currency. What it means: The Aussie rests on the inflation figures: a hot reading makes a November hike likely and supports it; a soft one pushes the hike out and leaves it exposed. The question to keep asking: is underlying inflation still running near 1% a quarter?
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: Australia's third-quarter inflation figures at 7:30 PM CT Tuesday (trimmed mean about +1.0% on the quarter expected), and the Reserve Bank of Australia decision on November 3.

scenarios.base: The Aussie holds near 70 cents until Tuesday night's inflation figures.
scenarios.bull: Hotter-than-expected inflation makes a November hike likely and lifts the Aussie.
scenarios.bear: Softer inflation pushes the hike out and pulls the Aussie back below 70 cents.

chapters.title: Canadian Dollar
chapters.teaser: The loonie held near 1.40 per US dollar even as oil fell about 6%, which usually hurts it. Markets still expect the Bank of Canada to raise rates on Wednesday, though two banks, TD Securities and Rabobank, now expect a hold.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: The Canadian dollar rose for seven straight days last week, to its strongest in about a month, helped by high oil and bets that the Bank of Canada hikes on October 28 because energy is pushing inflation up. What changed: Oil's drop on the Tehran peace efforts took away some of that support, with US crude near $101 from about $103 on Friday, but the loonie barely moved. A Bank of Canada hike is still priced at about 75–80%. Separately, US tariff changes on some Canadian goods, signed Friday, take effect on October 30. What it means: Much of a hike is already in the loonie's price, so a hike alone may not lift it much, while a hold would be a real surprise. The question to keep asking: does Bank of Canada governor Tiff Macklem raise rates and signal more?
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: the Bank of Canada decision and Monetary Policy Report at 8:45 AM CT Wednesday, with Macklem's press conference after; Canada's August GDP comes Friday at 7:30 AM CT.

scenarios.base: The loonie stays near 1.40 into Wednesday's decision.
scenarios.bull: A hike with a signal of more pushes the loonie toward 1.39 per dollar.
scenarios.bear: A hold, or a further oil slide, pushes the US dollar back toward 1.41 Canadian.

chapters.title: New Zealand Dollar
chapters.teaser: The kiwi held near 57.2 US cents ahead of the Reserve Bank of New Zealand decision at 8:00 PM CT on Tuesday, where a rate hike is widely expected.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: New Zealand's central bank is expected to raise its rate to 3.00% from 2.75% on October 28, because inflation, at 3.7%, is still above its target, and that expectation has supported the kiwi. What changed: Nothing new from New Zealand today. The kiwi firmed about 0.3% in Asian trading as the hike bets held, and lower oil eased pressure on an economy that imports its fuel. What it means: With a hike mostly priced, what the bank says about further hikes matters more than the move itself. The question to keep asking: does the bank signal more hikes beyond this one?
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: the Reserve Bank of New Zealand decision at 8:00 PM CT Tuesday, then the ANZ business confidence survey at 7:00 PM CT Wednesday.

chapters.title: Oil
chapters.teaser: Brent crude fell about 6% to near $110 a barrel, from about $117 on Friday, as Saudi Arabia's defence minister, Pakistan's army chief and Turkey's intelligence chief went to Tehran to stop the fighting flaring again.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: Oil has stayed high since the US–Iran war began in February, and Houthi attacks on Saudi oil sites drove Brent to a six-month high last week. What changed: The weekend passed without a US strike on Iran, Qatari mediators were in Tehran with US backing, and on Monday three regional delegations arrived to press for calm. Yemen's Houthi rebels said they hit pumping stations on Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline, but Saudi Arabia has not confirmed it and prices kept falling. US crude fell to about $101. What it means: Some of the war premium in oil is leaving the price. That helps energy importers like Japan and the euro area, and takes some support from oil exporters like Canada. The question to keep asking: do the Tehran talks produce anything concrete, or do the attacks resume?
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: any result from the Tehran talks, the American Petroleum Institute's weekly oil stocks at 3:30 PM CT Tuesday, and official US stocks figures at 9:30 AM CT Wednesday.
numbers: No US strike over the weekend; delegations in Tehran Monday

chapters.title: Gold
chapters.teaser: Gold held just above $4,000 an ounce, up about 0.3%, after falling last week to its lowest in about three months. A slightly weaker dollar helped, but expectations of a December US rate hike keep the bounce small.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: Gold fell nearly 4% last week as high oil raised fears of more inflation and more US rate hikes; gold pays no interest, so it suffers when rates rise. What changed: Falling oil and a slightly softer dollar let gold steady near $4,008. The calmer mood around Iran cut demand for safe assets, which limited the bounce. What it means: Cheaper oil eases the rate-hike pressure that hurt gold last week, which helps it; calmer geopolitics take away some of the safety demand, which hurts it. The question to keep asking: what does the Federal Reserve signal about December on Wednesday?
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: US consumer confidence at 9:00 AM CT Tuesday, then the Fed decision at 1:00 PM CT Wednesday.

calls.note: Oct 19: swaps now put an October 30 hike under 5% (BBH), below the ~25% in the call. December ~80% unchanged. October hike odds fell to about 4%, far below the ~25% in the call; Japan's inflation came in at 2.1% as expected and December (~80%) is now the meeting that matters.

calls.text: France's revenue-section budget vote Tue: a clean pass narrows the French–German spread (~141bp); a defeat or big concessions widens it and weighs on the euro
calls.note: No vote on Tuesday: it was pushed to October 27, so neither branch played out.

calls.text: UK jobs Tue 1 AM CT (earnings ~3.8% expected): sticky pay firms the BoE hike case before Wednesday's inflation; cooling pay backs Bailey's calmer view
calls.note: Sticky side won: unemployment fell to 4.7% (4.9% expected) and regular pay rose 3.7% (3.6% expected); total pay and claims were softer. Pound +0.3% to ~1.334.

calls.text: Konarak follow-through: a US confirmation or more strikes keeps oil's supply premium and lifts US yields; silence lets the morning's waiver drop resume
calls.note: No confirmation (a US official denied the strike) and no new strike overnight, yet the premium held: Brent ~$109.8 Tuesday on low Gulf flows and Iran's Hormuz claims. The waiver-driven drop did not resume.

calls.text: BoC Oct 28 with ~87% priced for a hike: a hike is mostly in the loonie already; a hold would be the surprise and hit it
NZ Q3 CPI Wed 4:45pm CT (~3.8% y/y): near forecast keeps the ~80% hike pricing; clearly soft reopens the hold and weighs on the kiwi
calls.note: Near forecast (3.7% vs 3.8%) and hike pricing held, rising to about 98%; the kiwi dipped only briefly.
